title: Research Universal VTT (UVTT) as the Tier 2 import format candidate, connecting it to the already-designed vision/dynamic-lighting mechanism
objective: Owner chose to move to the next open-source-options research area after Rules/Characters; this covers the Tier 2 (import) open item from docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md, which had zero research done. Found via WebSearch/WebFetch: Universal VTT (UVTT, also .dd2vtt/.df2vtt -- same format, different tool-of-origin extensions) is a JSON-in-image map-interchange format created by Megasploot (Wonderdraft/Dungeondraft's developer) and widely supported across competing commercial VTTs (Foundry, Fantasy Grounds Unity, Roll20, AboveVTT, Arkenforge, plus map-authoring tools Dungeon Alchemist/DungeonFog/BBEG Maps). Its schema (Resolution/map_origin/map_size/pixels_per_grid, a line_of_sight wall-segment array, objects_line_of_sight, a portals array with position/bounds/rotation/closed/freestanding, an environment block with baked_lighting/ambient_light, a lights array with position/range/intensity/color/shadows, and a base64-encoded PNG/WEBP image) maps directly onto the vision/dynamic-lighting mechanism already designed in docs/research/vtt-rules-and-character-system-options.md's 'Proposed consolidated agnostic architecture' section (VisionSource-style point-source polygon computation against wall geometry) -- meaning supporting UVTT import gives a genuinely interactive map (working walls/lights/doors) on day one, not just a static picture. Important honesty check: the format has no official public specification document, license, or governance body -- it is a de facto, community-documented convention (Arkenforge/Roll20-wiki/Dungeondraft-encyclopedia blog posts describe the same field set independently), not a formally licensed open standard. Parsing a JSON data-format convention is a different (and safer) situation than reusing someone's copyrighted source code, but this is recorded honestly rather than overclaimed as a governed standard.
validations: Added a 'Import format (Tier 2): Universal VTT (UVTT)' subsection to docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md documenting the format's schema, its wide adoption across competing commercial VTTs, its lack of formal governance/license (recorded honestly), and the direct connection to the already-designed vision/dynamic-lighting mechanism from the rules/character document.
